sources.quote: Each year, the OSHA carcinogens released into air in the highest quantities were styrene, acetaldehyde, and formaldehyde.
sources.searcher_note: National pattern only: styrene is the top carcinogen released to air; same page says 2023 styrene air releases came mainly from plastics product manufacturing and boat building. No California or facility breakdown. Date is the page's last-updated date as reported by the fetch; analysis covers 2023 data.

notes: No source found that names California's fiberglass/composite shops as a share of the state's cancer-listed air pounds, or the 40% / 55% figures. Only national pattern coverage (EPA TRI National Analysis: styrene top air carcinogen, from plastics and boat building). A 2018 Prop 65 settlement PDF on oag.ca.gov (2018-00607S9056) was surfaced by search as covering styrene from LA-area fiberglass facilities, but the PDF is scanned and could not be read, so it is not recorded. No coverage dated after 2026-06-30 found beyond the EPA page's update date. No source found that disagrees.
